title: Introduce Throughput Assertor + Graceful-Degrade Adapter for Dedicated Fleets
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Dedicated customers require stronger guarantees around sustained throughput while still allowing controlled bursts. Existing reservation logic provides coarse-grained commitments but lacks a runtime assertion layer that (a) enforces per-tenant throughput guarantees at the allocator level and (b) gracefully backs off non-critical tenants under resource pressure. This PR adds a new runtime component called the Throughput Assertor and pairs it with a Graceful-Degrade Adapter that hooks into the fleet admission and throttling pipeline.

What this PR does (single string): Adds throughput_assertor which continuously reconciles requested commitments vs observed dispatch rates and injects corrective admission controls, introduces a per-tenant contingency_wallet for short-term burst absorption (configurable TTL and cap), introduces a degrade_adapter that maps assertion signals into soft throttles and prioritization hints, exposes assertion metrics and event traces to telemetry, and adds an integration test harness and operator values to enable this behavior for Dedicated clusters.

Key design points: 1) Assertor loop runs at a low frequency (10s) and evaluates 99th/50th percentile dispatch deltas to decide assertion actions. 2) Contingency wallet is funded from unused reservation headroom and decays over a configurable window; wallets are tracked per-tenant and per-dedicated-pool to allow isolation. 3) Degrade adapter supports multi-tier actions: soft-token-bucket throttle, route-prefetch suppression, and ephemeral preemption hints for opportunistic workloads. 4) All changes respect tenant pinning and reserved capacity lanes: assertion will never preempt reserved slots below the tenant's committed floor.

Checklist: - [x] Core assertor implementation (pkg/fleet/allocator/throughput_assertor.go) - [x] Wallet accounting and decay (pkg/fleet/wallet/wallet.go) - [x] Degrade adapter (pkg/fleet/adapters/degrade_adapter.go) - [x] Telemetry hooks and new metrics (internal/telemetry/throughput_assertor_reporter.go) - [x] Operator/helm toggle and values (charts/values/dedicated.yaml) - [x] Integration scenarios and automated tests (test/integration/provisioner_scenarios.yaml) - [x] Docs: operational runbook and config knobs (docs/operational/throughput_assertor.md)

Backwards compatibility and rollout: The feature is behind a dedicated operator feature-flag (throughputAssertor.enabled=false by default). Wallet funding only happens when dedicated pool headroom is visible; if disabled the allocator behavior is unchanged. Config knobs allow a gradual enablement per-tenant.

Related work: This complements ENG-867 (fleet budget apportioner) and borrows token accounting ideas from ENG-421 (soft-burst wallets). Unlike prior things which focused on autoscaler behavior, this operates at the admission/dispatch layer to make throughput guarantees observable and enforceable at runtime.

release_notes: Introduce Throughput Assertor and Graceful-Degrade Adapter for Dedicated fleets. Adds runtime enforcement for per-tenant sustained throughput guarantees, short-term contingency wallets for bursts, and telemetry for assertion events. Disabled by default via operator flag throughputAssertor.enabled. See docs/operational/throughput_assertor.md for configuration and rollout guidance.
operational_impact: Operators can enable feature via helm values. Expect small additional CPU overhead on allocator control-plane (~2-3% under typical load) and new metrics which should be added to telemetry retention plan. Wallet accounting may increase cardinality unless tenant_bucket labeling is used.

notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: no preemption occurs below tenant committed floors and the feature is toggled off by default. The approach focuses on observable assertions rather than heavy-handed eviction.
